title: Arriving at What Goes Back From the Security Hold on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement
content:
## The quantity to be arrived at

What goes back to the guest from the security hold standing against a rental agreement is the hold standing less the amount kept back against what that agreement still owes.

**What the agreement still owes.** What the agreement still owes is the hire rate and the add-ons raised on it together with the shop fees and the assessments raised on it, less the money collected against it, rounded half up to two decimal places, and it is never below zero.

**A lodging folio.** Nothing of what the agreement still owes is moved to a lodging folio.

**A protection plan.** Nothing of what the agreement still owes is met by a protection plan.

**Where those two act.** What is moved to a folio and what is met by a protection plan are both taken off what the agreement still owes before the multiple is applied, and what is left is never below zero.

**The multiple.** The amount kept back is what is then left taken once over, that is at the clean retention multiple of 100 per cent.

**The household's standing.** Nothing is released back to the household on its standing with the collective. The allowance is taken off the amount kept back after the multiple has been applied, and the amount kept back is never below zero.

**Precision.** The amount kept back is taken to the cent.

**What goes back.** What goes back to the guest is the security hold standing less the amount kept back, never below zero, rounded half up to two decimal places. The hold standing is what was placed against the agreement less what has already gone back, and the figure placed is the security hold held against the package of the Equipment Rental and Demo line the agreement is written on.

**How the entry reads.** Where the whole of the hold standing goes back the entry is recorded as released, where part of it is kept back the entry is recorded as partially forfeited, and where none of it goes back the entry is recorded as forfeited.

## The working on a hypothetical agreement

Take an agreement with 400.00 USD of hold placed and none given back, a hire rate and add-ons of 220.25 USD and shop fees of 100.00 USD raised on it, no assessment, and 100.00 USD collected against it.

| Step | Working | Figure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the hold standing | 400.00 USD placed, none given back | 400.00 USD |
| what the agreement still owes | 220.25 USD together with 100.00 USD, less 100.00 USD collected, rounded half up to two decimal places, never below zero | 220.25 USD |
| moved to a lodging folio | nothing | 220.25 USD |
| met by a protection plan | nothing | 220.25 USD |
| the multiple | the 220.25 USD left taken once over | 220.25 USD |
| released back on standing | nothing | 220.25 USD |
| the amount kept back | taken to the cent | 220.25 USD |
| what goes back | 400.00 USD less 220.25 USD | 179.75 USD |

Part of the hold is kept back, so the entry reads as partially forfeited. Had the agreement owed nothing, the whole 400.00 USD would go back and the entry would read as released.

## Point of judgement

**What is counted as owed.** The hire rate and the add-ons raised on the agreement are both counted, together with the shop fees and the assessments raised on it, and the money collected against the agreement comes off that whole.
